examples.case_name: Example 1: Acute Coronary Syndrome (Red Flag Emergency)
examples.clinical_scenario: A 58-year-old male arrives via ambulance with substernal crushing chest pain, diaphoresis, acute hypotension (SBP 85 mmHg), and mild hypoxia (SpO2 91%).

examples.case_name: Example 2: Chronic Kidney Disease with Stage 2 Hypertension (Urgent)
examples.clinical_scenario: A 64-year-old female presenting with bilateral pitting pedal edema, fatigue, elevated serum creatinine (3.4 mg/dL), blood urea (78 mg/dL), and BP 155/96 mmHg.

examples.case_name: Example 3: Routine Diabetic Screening with Missing Liver Panel
examples.clinical_scenario: A 42-year-old asymptomatic male with family history of diabetes, fasting glucose 195 mg/dL, BMI 29.5 kg/m2, normal vitals, but liver function tests were not ordered.
